quote: and Bauer said, "That is not a confirmation. A voice is neither a callsign nor a tag. It is enough to reopen the file, and I am reopening it. My callsign limb I already hold: BERG 4, 15:55, one casualty in the couloir. That report was never wrong."
note: NOT a late finding, and recorded here because the critic-memory ledger is where the loop keeps what it learns about its critics. This is the instance LOOP-003 section 2 does not cover, asked for by name. The SCIENCE critic wrote the finding whose repair broke the OUTLINE critic's score. Science's attempt-1 finding read: 'Line 0471 is instead validated on a voice transmission from the subject himself and a tag-reconciliation analysis — neither of which is a field-team callsign report,' and proposed as its fix 'either have a field team radio in a callsign confirmation as the first input... or add a line establishing that a first-person voice transmission is an accepted equivalent.' The orchestrator wrote branch one into the level-1 sheet. The writer executed it exactly. Outline then reported: 'beat 7 — Bauer plays the 23:12 voice tape at 03:14 and takes it as his first confirmation, a voice not a tag — does not happen; the patched line has him explicitly reject the tape as a confirmation and substitute his existing BERG 4 callsign report, which is the opposite event.' Outline fell 10 to 7. Outline had been named on the sheet's DO NOT TOUCH list and the writer never touched it: the sentence that broke it was a sentence the sheet ordered changed. Two aggravations beyond the recorded precedent in last-lighthouse-keeper-on-titan ch01: the repair also lowered CONTINUITY from 5 to 4 by creating both of its next findings, and it lowered SCIENCE ITSELF from 5 to 4, so the critic that commissioned the repair scored the result worse than what it replaced.

quote: add a line establishing that a first-person voice transmission is an accepted equivalent to a field-team callsign under this post's procedures
note: Recorded against the ORCHESTRATOR, not a critic. Science's attempt-1 finding offered two branches and arbitration silently chose one without recording that a choice was being made. Branch two, quoted above, would have preserved outline beat 7 and was never tried on a draft. Asked afterwards, the science critic said branch two would also have failed — 'that is a definition, not a threshold a character can satisfy by asserting equivalence' — so the outcome was probably the same, but the loop should know that a level-1 sheet turned a critic's two-branch fix into a one-branch instruction with no record of the decision. The sheet template has no field for a finding whose fix has alternatives, and that is a gap in the format rather than in this run.

quote: and Bauer said, "A voice is neither a callsign nor a tag, so the tape itself is not the limb. But it is what reopens the file, and reopening it I enter my first confirmation now: BERG 4, 15:55, one casualty in the couloir. Callsign limb, confirmed 03:14."
note: Worth keeping in this critic's favour. Arbitration selected the outline critic's own reconciliation text and applied it verbatim, then asked that critic to score the result and told it plainly not to score it higher than it believed because the text was its own. It returned 7 and marked beat 7 missing — against its own sentence. It had predicted exactly that in the arbitration round, saying it would score the reconciliation present-with-caveat rather than present. A critic that inflates its own text would have made this run halt on a false 8 or pass on a false 10; this one did neither.
